accepted.question_text: For an infinite-dimensional control system, suppose a continuous Lyapunov function satisfies the ISS implication-form condition that whenever the state norm is at least a prescribed gain of the input norm, the Lie derivative is negative definite in the state norm. Does this implication-form condition always imply the dissipative-form ISS Lyapunov inequality, without imposing additional restrictive assumptions on the system or on the Lyapunov function?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.17. For infinite-dimensional systems, it is easy to see that if V is an ISS Lyapunov function in dissipative form, then it is an ISS Lyapunov function in implication form. It is, however, an open question, whether the converse implication holds unless quite restrictive requirements on Σ and Lyapunov function V are imposed, see [167, Theorem 3.4].

accepted.question_text: Can one prove local input-to-state stability from non-coercive Lyapunov functions in the infinite-dimensional setting, in particular for non-coercive Lyapunov functions stated in implication form rather than only in dissipative form?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.21. Theorem 2.19, in contrast to Theorem 2.18, gives an ISS criterion only for the global ISS property, and non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions are formulated in dissipative form. Currently, there are no non-coercive Lyapunov results for the LISS property and for non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions defined in implication form.

accepted.question_text: Given an infinite-dimensional system that is locally input-to-state stable, can one derive a precise, constructive description of the region in the state-input space X × U on which a particular LISS estimate with prescribed comparison functions β and γ is guaranteed to hold?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.26. The proof of Theorem 2.25 is based on converse Lyapunov theorems for the 0-UAS property, see [161], and thus it does not give a precise estimate for the region in X ×U for which the LISS estimate (1.6) is valid (for given β, γ). The estimation of the region in which the LISS estimate is valid is a hard problem, which has not been touched so far for infinite-dimensional systems.

accepted.question_text: Do general nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems, and in particular general linear boundary control systems, admit converse ISS Lyapunov theorems guaranteeing the existence of coercive ISS Lyapunov functions whenever the system is ISS?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.28. For general nonlinear systems and even for general linear boundary control systems converse ISS Lyapunov theorems are not available now and constitute an important and complex open problem.

accepted.question_text: For infinite-dimensional linear systems with input space L∞(R+, U), does input-to-state stability always imply integral input-to-state stability, even though the reverse implication is known and finite-dimensional intuition suggests a positive answer?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3.22. In view of Proposition 3.20 we know that for U := L∞(R+, U), integral ISS implies ISS. At the same time, the question whether ISS w.r.t. L∞(R+, U) implies iISS w.r.t. L∞(R+, U) is a challenging open problem.

accepted.question_text: For linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators, does ISS always imply the existence of an ISS Lyapunov function, and in particular do coercive ISS Lyapunov functions exist for Dirichlet heat equations or, more generally, for analytic-semigroup systems generated by operators with unbounded spectrum?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3.31. In spite of several positive results described in this section, our present knowledge of Lyapunov methods for linear systems with unbounded operators is insufficient, and many questions are open. The very first question is whether ISS of (3.1) implies the existence of a (coercive or non-coercive) ISS Lyapunov function. It is known that for linear hyperbolic systems of conservation laws it is possible to construct a coercive ISS Lyapunov function [216], and at the time it is unknown, whether coercive ISS Lyapunov functions exist for a heat equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions, or, more generally, for systems governed by analytic semigroups generated by operators with an unbounded spectrum.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove an ISS estimate for Burgers' equation on (0,1) with boundary condition x(t,0)=0, disturbed boundary input x(t,1)=u(t), state space L2(0,1), and bounded piecewise-continuous inputs, without imposing the small-input restriction sup_t |u(t)| ≤ μ/ν?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.12. Is it possible to prove ISS of Burgers’ equation (5.40)-(5.41) with X := L2(0, 1) and u ∈ P Cb(R+, R) (or for another input space) without restrictions on the magnitude of inputs?

accepted.question_text: For disturbance-to-state stabilization of linear hyperbolic systems by dynamic boundary feedback, can the restrictive matrix inequality condition (5.52b), introduced to compensate for the lack of proportional gain, be relaxed or replaced by different criteria that still guarantee the desired robustness result?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.22. In the statement of Theorem 5.18, condition (5.52a) requires infD∈Dn+ kD(H +BK)D−1k < 1 which also appears in the more general context of nonlinear systems [43] when analyzing stability with respect to H2-norm. However, the condition (5.52b) is introduced in [215] to compensate for the lack of proportional gain in the feedback law. It definitely restricts the class of systems that can be treated with this approach and relaxing this condition or obtaining different criteria is a topic of further investigation.

accepted.question_text: For infinite networks of interconnected ISS systems with nonlinear gains, what are the precise relationships among spectral small-gain conditions, robust strong small-gain conditions, the existence of an Ω-path for the gain operator, and monotone invertibility of id − Γ, and how can those relationships be used to obtain decisive ISS small-gain theorems?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6.12. Small-gain results presented in this section use various types of the small-gain conditions: spectral small-gain condition [123], robust strong small-gain condition [53], existence of a so-called Ω-path for a gain operator Γ [53], as well as “monotone invertibility” of id −Γ [164]. The relations between these conditions are known for finite networks, but are unclear for infinite networks. Understanding of these relationships and using of this knowledge to obtain ISS small-gain theorems for infinite networks with nonlinear gains is a challenging open problem.

accepted.question_text: For retarded time-delay systems in the infinite-dimensional ISS framework, are forward completeness and bounded reachability sets equivalent, and are the non-uniform limit property LIM and the uniform limit property ULIM actually equivalent notions?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7.5. Although the ISS Superposition theorem (Theorem 2.7) is valid for time-delay systems, it is possible that for time-delay systems tighter results can be obtained. In particular, it is not known whether forward completeness and boundedness of reachability sets are equivalent properties for time-delay systems (for the ODE case such a claim is true [143] and for general infinite-dimensional systems it is false [172]), and whether LIM and ULIM properties are equivalent notions, see [171] for more detailed discussions on this topic.

accepted.question_text: For ISS Lyapunov-Krasovskii functionals of time-delay systems, can the standard dissipation requirement V(x) ≥ χ(|u(0)|) ⇒ V̇_u(x) ≤ −α(|x(0)|) be weakened to the pointwise state-threshold condition |x(0)| ≥ χ(‖u‖_U) ⇒ V̇_u(x) ≤ −α(|x(0)|) while still guaranteeing ISS?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7.9. A question whether it is possible to weaken the requirement (7.9) further to merely (7.10) |x(0)| ≥ χ(kukU) ⇒ V˙u(x) ≤ −α(|x(0)|), remains open, see [36] for some preliminary results and [35] for the positive answer of the closely related question for the iISS property.

accepted.question_text: Can one develop a substantial input-to-output stability theory for infinite-dimensional systems, analogous to the well-developed finite-dimensional IOS theory, beyond the few currently known results such as some small-gain theorems and delay-system results?

evidence.quote: For finite-dimensional systems the IOS theory is quite rich, see, e.g., [4, 212, 222]. There is almost no result on IOS theory in the context of infinite-dimensional systems (except for delay systems). Some exceptions include the small-gain results for IOS systems in [12, 111].

accepted.question_text: Can one build general ISS methods for fully nonlinear infinite-dimensional PDEs, such as porous medium and Navier-Stokes type equations, that do not fit the semilinear template ẋ = Ax + f(x,u) with a bounded nonlinear part on bounded balls?

evidence.quote: However, many important PDEs as porous medium equation [230] and Navier-Stokes equations, do not fall into this category. This calls for looking onto a more general class of infinite-dimensional problems, which will include fully nonlinear PDEs. For systems without inputs, the theory of nonlinear semigroups [44, 122, 159] gives a powerful method for the unified study of such equations. General methods for investigation of ISS for systems from this class are highly desirable.

accepted.question_text: How can ISS techniques be turned into practical robust-control design methods for infinite-dimensional systems, especially for boundary or in-domain controller synthesis in challenging applications where current H∞ or transfer-function approaches do not yet provide a complete answer?

evidence.quote: Many open control problems exist in the literature for robust control designs, as the drilling problem (see [193] and references therein), and the flexible structure control in aircraft (see in particular [60, 189]) to point out only a few robust control problems. Use of ISS techniques for robust control design is, to a large extent, still an open problem.
